case.case_title: Weerawansha and others vs. Attorney-General and others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports (2006) 1 Sri L R. SC FR 228/2005, decided on 15 July 2005

clause.text: No citizen shall be discriminated against on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth or any one of such grounds.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the MoU discriminated against citizens outside the six tsunami-affected districts by restricting relief and committee functions, thus infringing Article 12(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioners claimed the MoU discriminated against citizens outside the six districts who were equally or worse affected by the tsunami, on grounds of place of birth and residence, violating Article 12(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents argued the MoU was designed to provide urgent humanitarian assistance specifically to the six districts most affected, and the structure was necessary and lawful under the circumstances.
key_facts: The MoU limited tsunami relief management to six specified districts.
The Regional Committee was located in Kilinochchi, an LTTE-controlled area.
Citizens outside these districts who were affected were excluded from the relief structure.
The petitioners alleged discrimination based on place of birth and residence.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court recognized that Article 12(2) prohibits discrimination on grounds including place of birth and residence. The court found that the MoU's limitation of relief and committee functions to six districts, and the location of the Regional Committee in an inaccessible area, constituted discrimination against other affected citizens.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court held that the exclusion of other equally or worse affected citizens outside the six districts from the relief structure was discriminatory. The location of the Regional Committee in Kilinochchi further exacerbated this discrimination by limiting access.
principles_established: Discrimination on grounds of place of birth or residence in relief efforts violates constitutional guarantees.
Relief and administrative structures must ensure equitable access to all affected persons.

outcome.holding: The court granted interim relief to stay the operation of the provision locating the Regional Committee in Kilinochchi and required parties to select a more accessible site, addressing the discrimination under Article 12(2).
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Stay on the location of the Regional Committee in Kilinochchi; parties to decide a suitable, centrally located site accessible to all affected persons.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(2) was materially engaged as the petitioners challenged the MoU for discriminating against citizens outside the six districts on grounds of place of birth and residence, which the court found to be a valid constitutional concern.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioners contended that the MoU discriminates against citizens outside the six districts who have been equally or worse affected by the tsunami on the basis of place of birth and residence, infringing Article 12(2). The court found a strong prima facie case and granted interim relief restraining the operation of the provision locating the Regional Committee in Kilinochchi.
